title: Jamestown man named in secret indictment for May shooting - NewsBreak
text: ( WJET/WFXP )– Prosecutors in Chautauqua County have accused a Jamestown, New York, man of pulling the trigger in a shooting that happened earlier this year. Jamestown police and the Chautauqua County District Attorney announced the unsealing of a secret indictment of 19-year-old Marquan Cunningham-Carper of Jamestown, charging him with first-degree assault and two counts of second-degree criminal possession of a weapon. That shooting happened back on May 8 in the area of North Hopkins Avenue and East 2nd Street, striking one person several times in the back, who received treatment and was later released from the hospital. Cunningham-Carper was arraigned Tuesday in Chautauqua County Court and pleaded not guilty, with bail being set at $1 million cash or 2 million property bond or $2 million partially secured by the posting of 10%. If convicted, he faces up to 25 years in prison and five years of supervised release. Chautauqua County District Attorney Jason Schmidt released a statement saying: “Every single shooting incident and illegal possession and use of a gun in our community hurts us all. This instance – the indiscriminate shooting in the backside of a young man who was merely walking home after shopping at a nearby store – says it all about where we stand as a community and the police’s ongoing fight, in which they are outgunned and outnumbered, to keep us safe and rid our streets of violent offenders. Today’s unsealing of the indictment against Mr. Cunningham-Carper is just the first step in the litigation which lies ahead for us. From the moment of the first 911 call received by Jamestown Police, it’s investigators along with ours at the DA’s Office have worked diligently to develop evidence identifying the shooter and allowing us to move forward with this prosecution. We elected to bring our investigation into the Grand Jury due to the seriousness of the crimes committed here and our concerns for public safety, but the investigation still continues and we anticipate developing further evidence enhancing the case. Mr. Cunningham-Carper is presumed innocent under the law. If convicted, he faces a maximum prison term of 25 years followed by 5 years of parole supervision. We now move on to the discovery and motion stages of our prosecution, with a conference set for July 21 st . I urge anyone with information concerning the shooting to contact Jamestown Police or my office.” For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WWLP.
